c.tagline: Karnataka's regal city of palaces, sandalwood, silk, and yoga.

taxi.fareNote: Auto-rickshaws rarely use the meter and need firm negotiation before boarding; app-cabs (Uber, Ola, Rapido) and prepaid counters give the most predictable, honest fares.

emergency.note: 112 is India's single all-in-one emergency number connecting police, fire, and ambulance; 108 is the dedicated ambulance line and 100 reaches police directly.

avoid.reason: Expect rickshaw overcharging and pushy sandalwood-oil and incense 'factory' detours around the palace and Devaraja Market.

hood_desc: The walkable heart of Mysore around the illuminated Mysore Palace, with Sayyaji Rao Road's shops, hotels, and eateries close at hand; the natural base for first-timers who want the main sights on the doorstep.

The bustling old bazaar quarter around the vibrant Devaraja Market, piled with flowers, spices, sandalwood, and produce; a lively, local, budget-friendly area for those who want the city at street level.

A leafy, upscale western suburb that is Mysore's yoga capital, drawing Ashtanga students from around the world to its studios, healthy cafes, and calm tree-lined streets; suits longer, laid-back stays.
A well-planned, affluent residential district near the university and the birdlife-rich Kukkarahalli Lake; green, quiet, and popular with families and long-stay visitors.
A residential area on the eastern side near Mysore Zoo and Karanji Lake at the foot of Chamundi Hill; calm and convenient for the zoo and the hill temple.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only.

transit.hours: KSRTC and city buses run from roughly 5:30 AM to 10:00 PM; auto-rickshaws and app-cabs cover late-night gaps.
transit.note: Mysore has no metro or suburban rail — the KSRTC city bus network (hubbed at the City and Suburban bus stands) is the backbone of public transport, supplemented by ubiquitous auto-rickshaws and app-cabs (Uber, Ola, Rapido). The compact, grid-planned center is very walkable.
transit.pay: Pay bus fares in cash to the conductor (a few rupees per hop); auto-rickshaws should run the meter or be booked by app, and app-cabs are cashless or cash. There is no citywide smart-card system.

air: Kempegowda International Airport Bengaluru (BLR, ~170 km — main gateway)
bus: KSRTC intercity buses (Central & Suburban Bus Stands)
train: Mysuru Junction (Indian Railways — frequent trains to Bengaluru)

transit.m: Prepaid or app taxi (Uber/Ola) to city center (~20-30 min)
Auto-rickshaw from the airport road to the city (~30 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants is appreciated, and a small tip to drivers and porters is common.

food.name: Mysore masala dosa
food.desc: A soft, butter-soaked dosa smeared inside with fiery red garlic chutney and folded over spiced potato, eaten with coconut chutney rather than sambar.

places.name: Original Vinayaka Mylari
places.note: Legendary hole-in-the-wall whose thick, spongy butter dosa is the version locals argue about.

places.name: Hotel Dasaprakash
places.note: Institution running since the 1920s, with a large pure-vegetarian dining hall and consistent tiffin.

places.name: Hotel RRR
places.note: Busy all-day tiffin house near the palace, handy for a dosa before or after sightseeing.

food.name: Mysore pak
food.desc: The city's gift to India: gram flour cooked with sugar and a lot of ghee until it sets into a porous, melting fudge; invented in the palace kitchen.

places.name: Guru Sweet Mart
places.area: Sayyaji Rao Road, by Devaraja Market
places.note: Run by descendants of the palace cook credited with inventing Mysore pak; sold warm by weight.

places.name: Bombay Tiffanys
places.note: Long-established sweet shop known for its Mysore pak and its own signature Bombay toast.

places.name: Devaraja Market sweet stalls
places.note: Several counters inside and around the old market sell fresh batches to compare.

food.name: Bisi bele bath
food.desc: Karnataka's hot lentil-and-rice one-pot, thick with tamarind, vegetables and a roasted masala, finished with ghee and crunchy boondi.

places.name: Hotel Dasaprakash
places.note: Classic vegetarian dining room where the meal plates and rice dishes are the mainstay.

places.name: Mahesh Prasad
places.note: Popular pure-veg spot for South Indian rice dishes and thalis at everyday prices.

places.name: Hotel RRR
places.note: Serves it as part of a broad Karnataka menu including banana-leaf meals.

food.name: Chiroti
food.desc: Paper-thin layered pastry deep-fried until it shatters, dusted with powdered sugar and traditionally eaten soaked in warm saffron-cardamom milk.

places.name: Guru Sweet Mart
places.area: Sayyaji Rao Road, by Devaraja Market
places.note: Makes the flaky festival sweets alongside its famous Mysore pak, fresh through the day.

places.name: Bombay Tiffanys
places.note: Reliable counter for chiroti and other Karnataka sweets, with boxes for taking away.

places.name: Hotel Dasaprakash
places.note: Serves chiroti with badam milk as a dessert, the traditional pairing.

food.name: Mysore-style mutton pulao
food.desc: The city's rare non-vegetarian classic: short-grain rice cooked with mutton, coconut and a mild green masala, served with onion salad and a thin curry.

places.name: Hanumanthu Restaurant
places.note: The name locals give first for Mysore mutton pulao; simple room, decades of practice, sells out early.

places.name: Hotel Ayub Bawarchi
places.note: Old Muslim-quarter kitchen turning out pulao, biryani and kebabs; the neighbourhood for meat here.

places.name: Mandi Mohalla food street
places.note: Cluster of pulao and kebab stalls that come alive in the evening, especially in Ramadan.

food.name: Idli, vada and kesari bath
food.desc: The Mysore breakfast trio: pillowy steamed idli, crisp lentil vada and sweet saffron semolina kesari bath, all with coconut chutney.

places.name: Mahesh Prasad
places.note: Reliable morning tiffin counter with fast turnover, so everything arrives hot.

places.name: Hotel Dasaprakash
places.note: Old-school breakfast hall serving the full tiffin range from early morning.

places.name: Original Vinayaka Mylari
places.note: Tiny menu done exceptionally well; go early because it closes between sittings.

food.name: Mysore filter coffee
food.desc: Chicory-blended coffee dripped through a steel filter, frothed with hot milk and poured between tumbler and davara until it foams; the day starts with this.

places.name: Indra Cafe Paras
places.note: Long-running city cafe where the filter coffee is the reason regulars keep coming back.

places.name: Hotel Dasaprakash
places.note: Serves the coffee in the traditional tumbler and davara, unchanged for generations.

places.name: Cafe Aramane
places.note: Convenient stop by the palace gates for a strong filter coffee and a quick snack.

food.name: Badam milk
food.desc: Almond milk simmered with saffron, cardamom and sugar, drunk hot in the evening or chilled in summer; a Mysore sweet-shop counter staple.

places.name: Guru Sweet Mart
places.area: Sayyaji Rao Road, by Devaraja Market
places.note: Made fresh alongside the sweets, and the natural chaser to a slab of Mysore pak.

places.name: Bombay Tiffanys
places.note: Sweet shop counter serving badam milk and other milk drinks through the day.

places.name: Devaraja Market drink stalls
places.note: Cheap glasses served among the flower and spice aisles of the old market.

landmarks: Mysore Palace (Amba Vilas)
The Wodeyar maharajas' Indo-Saracenic masterpiece dazzles with stained glass, gilded domes, and 100,000 lightbulbs that blaze on Sunday nights.
Chamundi Hill and Chamundeshwari Temple
A thousand steps climb past a giant Nandi to this hilltop temple of Mysore's patron goddess, with sweeping views over the city.
Brindavan Gardens
Terraced symmetrical gardens below the Krishna Raja Sagara dam erupt each evening with illuminated musical fountains, a beloved excursion since the 1930s.
Devaraja Market
A century-old bazaar overflowing with jasmine garlands, pyramids of kumkum powder, bananas, and Mysore silk, delivering photogenic chaos in the city center.
St. Philomena's Cathedral
Twin 53-meter neo-Gothic spires modeled on Cologne Cathedral rise above one of India's largest churches, sheltering a relic of the saint in its crypt.
Monolithic Nandi Statue, Chamundi Hill
Carved from a single black granite boulder in 1659, this five-meter sacred bull remains garlanded and venerated on the pilgrim steps.
Jaganmohan Palace Art Gallery
A former royal palace houses Raja Ravi Varma paintings, rare musical instruments, and treasures of the Wodeyar collection behind its ornate facade.
Mysore Zoo (Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens)
Founded in 1892, one of India's oldest and best-kept zoos parades tigers, gorillas, and giraffes through spacious landscaped grounds.
Srirangapatna
Tipu Sultan's island fortress capital nearby preserves his summer palace Daria Daulat, the Ranganathaswamy temple, and battle-scarred ramparts on the Kaveri.
Karanji Lake
A tranquil lake at Chamundi's foot features India's largest walk-through aviary and hosts painted storks, pelicans, and butterflies.

train.note: No international trains. Mysuru Junction is about 2 km from the palace, and the Vande Bharat and Shatabdi services cover the Bengaluru run in around two hours, making it an easy day trip. Longer-distance trains reach Chennai and the Kerala coast. Book on IRCTC 60 days ahead; the Bengaluru trains are commuter-busy on Friday and Sunday.

bus.note: No international coaches. KSRTC Karnataka (https://ksrtc.karnataka.gov.in/) runs very frequent buses from the central and suburban bus stands to Bengaluru (about 3 hours), Ooty, Coorg and Hassan, with private coaches on redBus (https://www.redbus.in/). Buses are more frequent than trains to Bengaluru but slower.

ferry.note: Mysuru is inland on the Deccan plateau, so there are no ferries. Coracle rides on the Kaveri at Srirangapatna nearby are a local novelty rather than transport.

half.name: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
half.blurb: A river-island bird sanctuary on the Kaveri where painted storks, herons, and other migratory birds nest each season.

half.name: Bandipur National Park
half.blurb: A tiger reserve and UNESCO biosphere on the Karnataka-Tamil Nadu border, home to elephants and deer in dry deciduous forest.

half.name: Gaganachukki and Barachukki Falls
half.blurb: Twin waterfalls on the Kaveri River near Shivanasamudra, split into two separate cascades on either side of the island.

full.name: Belur and Halebidu
full.blurb: Two Hoysala-era temple towns with elaborately carved stone shrines dating to the 12th century.
